body.statement: For a stationary binary-endpoint reanalysis of a logged real-time adaptive trial whose inferior-arm probabilities satisfy the two-sided rare-arm envelope and whose endpoint delays satisfy the polynomial envelope, compute the risk-difference statistic from records observed through \(H_T=T+\Delta_T\). A protocol seeking a uniformly honest guarantee over this informative-delay envelope class cannot prespecify \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm W}\) unless \(T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\to0\). When the regular-variance condition is also verified, this condition is sufficient for ordinary Wald; without that condition, use the hybrid \(I_{T,\Delta}\), which deploys \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}\) only behind its observable gate and otherwise uses \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\), or use \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\) alone. Extra prespecified follow-up may remove the tail obstruction, but returning to ordinary Wald still requires regular variance. This class-wide necessity does not preclude pointwise validity of ordinary Wald for particular laws, including laws with immediate delays.
body.justification: This translates the uniform theorem into an auditable protocol-level inference choice for delayed cardiovascular endpoints without imposing a necessity claim on each individual delay law or claiming the original simulations satisfy the assumptions.
body.gap: Liberali et al. report resampling intervals and inferior-arm precision costs but no uniform coverage theorem under outcome-dependent ascertainment.
body.consumer: A GUSTO-1 or EUROPA-style protocol can prespecify the tail pad or follow-up period needed for class-wide honesty after verifying the logged propensity and delay-tail envelopes, while permitting an ordinary-Wald pointwise analysis under a separately certified prompt-delay law.
body.proof_tex:
A stationary binary endpoint takes values in \([0,1]\subset[-1,1]\), and its risk difference is the causal contrast \(\tau=PY(1)-PY(0)\). Once the logged inferior-arm probabilities satisfy the two-sided rare-arm envelope and the ascertainment delays satisfy the polynomial envelope, the trial law belongs to the informative-delay model class. If
\[
 T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\not\longrightarrow0,
\]
the hidden-sign construction in the Wald frontier, with any fixed support-feasible variance floor, is a subfamily of this model class and disproves uniform honesty of the unpadded interval. This proves the proposition's class-wide necessary condition. In contrast, the uniform gated-inference theorem supplies the bias-aware Gaussian branch and concentration fallback from the same terminal records without a regular-variance premise, so either such a pad-and-fallback rule or additional prespecified follow-up is required for a class-wide guarantee when the displayed tail obstruction remains.

If the regular-variance condition is independently verified, the sufficiency half of the Wald frontier shows that the displayed product tending to zero is also sufficient for the ordinary interval. Without that variance condition, the Gaussian branch is used only behind the observable gate in \(I_{T,\Delta}\); the concentration branch alone is also valid by (2)--(3). Thus the corrected protocol rule does not silently apply a studentized Gaussian approximation in a degenerate regime.

The follow-up condition has the following explicit elbow. Since \(q=(1-\alpha)/2>0\),
\[
 T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\to0
\]
holds with \(\Delta_T=0\) whenever \(\beta>q\). If \(\beta=q\), it is equivalent to
\[
 \frac{\Delta_T}{T}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
If \(\beta<q\), it is equivalent to
\[
 T+\Delta_T\gg T^{q/\beta}.
\]
Finally, this is a uniform statement over the envelope class. At a particular prompt-delay law the hidden bias is zero, so the construction does not imply pointwise Wald failure there.
